tools.name: membrane_state
tools.description: The machine membrane, both directions: which foreign sources this institution can read and at what cost on the carrier ladder, and which machine consumers arrive here and what they were answered. A passport records how a source publishes and what our probes saw, never what its documents assert; a reader row records a declared identity, which is a claim and not a credential.

tools.name: foreign_discover
tools.description: Ask a domain how it wants to be read by machines, and record the answer. Probes robots, the document head, conventional addresses and .well-known, then names the cheapest carrier that can answer: push, feed, sitemap, structured metadata, or -- last -- HTML extraction. Use before watching any external source; fetching the page and interpreting it is the most expensive rung, not the default.

tools.name: sitemap_delta
tools.description: What moved on a source since last time: addresses added, changed by lastmod, and removed. Removed matters most -- a withdrawn address is a withdrawal of support for whatever it said, and every copy never told keeps asserting it. An unchanged sitemap costs a digest comparison.

from_robots_host.description: read the sitemaps robots declares instead

tools.name: institutional_measure
tools.description: Run a declared measurement against this institution and read its receipt: gym ceilings and residuals, representation preservation envelopes, resource admission decisions, funding closure and frontier, reconciliation consequences, identity closure under deformation, and the failure cohort. Which measurements exist is declared in the CMS, not compiled here, so a new one is a row rather than a release -- call it with op=list to see what this estate can currently measure. Every measurement is read-only: the runners write nothing and perform no effect. Cannot infer: a measured ceiling is not a promise, a residual is not a defect, and a computed consequence is not an approval.

subject.description: the instance to measure: a gym, an institution, a namespace

tools.name: architecture_atlas
tools.description: Query the canonical architecture registry: summary, search, get, cannot-infer, expand, loss. The registry is lossless and large; this is the cheap read path, so ask it rather than loading atlas.index.json into context.

arg.description: query for search, id for get/cannot_infer, view name for expand

tools.name: model_local_inventory
tools.description: What local generation is actually runnable here: the registered model catalogue, whether each model's weights are present on disk, and which native organs can run them. Ask this before routing bounded work locally, and when a remote provider is exhausted.

tools.name: model_local_generate
tools.description: Generate through a native local organ rather than a remote provider. Use when a mission constrains work to local paths, or when a provider returns credit_balance_exhausted. Refuses with the specific missing weight rather than falling back to a remote provider, because a silent fallback would violate the routing constraint that sent the work here.

tools.name: estate_query
tools.description: Read-only SQL over the mature receipted estate: 6.5M observations, hot SQLite rows shadowing cold Parquet, composed in one view. Tables: observation, page, parcel_flat. SELECT and WITH only.

sql.description: a single SELECT or WITH statement

tools.name: finance_book
tools.description: The service book every commerce grammar quotes from: each service, its carrying cost, its asking price, its margin, and whether it can actually be sold. An unpriced service is not free -- it answers not_for_sale to x402, MPP, UCP, ACP and Beckn alike.

tools.name: finance_price_set
tools.description: Price a service in the book. This is the one write that makes a capability sellable through every commerce grammar at once, because they all read this book.

tools.name: protocol_fetch
tools.description: Speak one of the live carrier protocols over the same institutional state. Carriers: x402, mpp, a2a, cloudevents, ogc, ogc_items, reso, mismo, activitypub, activitypub_outbox, webfinger, beckn, ucp, acp, wot, cap, epcis, openrtb. A protocol is a projection, never a second owner of the data, so two carriers cannot disagree about a price or a parcel. Carriers that answer empty do so with a stated reason rather than a sample record.

name.description: capability name, for x402 and mpp

tools.name: desk_open_decisions
tools.description: What the institution is holding open right now, computed from the stores that hold it: capabilities advertised without a price, notes written but not published, offers in the book at zero, and work started but not finished. Each count is counted, not inferred from a page size.

tools.name: studio_membrane_status
tools.description: Read the financial membrane: budget caps, recorded cost, and the service book, together.

tools.name: studio_membrane_budget_set
tools.description: Set a budget cap for a recipe on the financial membrane.

tools.name: studio_economy_cost_record
